## Behavior

This follow-up keeps literal shell arguments separate from syntax and preserves the screen's approval boundary. It retains the existing #30/#12/#3 follow-up, the imported #20 work, and the five external follow-up commits through `38d586ae3b2bce634e854990844f1db0b7642618`.

- **Cmd loops:** recognize a loop only in command position, delimit its input set before finding `do`, and require a body. Ordinary text such as `cmd /c echo ready for review` and directory names such as `do` stay literal. FOR /F file and literal inputs are distinguished from command sources. Supported `usebackq` forms preserve their quote semantics; attached keyword spellings observed to execute a command conservatively require review. Computed inputs, malformed loops, nested execution, and refused programs retain their existing review or blocking paths.
- **POSIX expansions:** determine whether a quoted parameter expands to multiple fields from the actual parameter expression. Literal `{@` or `{!prefix@` inside a scalar fallback no longer causes a false review. Real `${@}`, positional slices, and indirect prefix expansion keep their multi-field controls.
- **Wrapper arguments:** parse grouped `command` lookup switches and stop `env` option parsing at the correct boundary. A lone `-` before assignments is an option; after an assignment it is the executable name. The latter no longer causes an argument such as `./brew.exe` to be mistaken for the program being run.
- **fd classification:** retain attached filter values as data, including `-tf` and `--type=f`, while later execution actions remain mutable. The read-only helper accepts these literal data forms only after the screen returns Clear; assignment prefixes, redirection, and execution controls remain covered.

The current-head reconciliation preserves all 25 added external test statements, except the one expectation contradicted by authentic `env` execution: `env GROUP=value - ./brew.exe install fixture` now expects Clear because the executed program is the literal `-`. New adjacent tests preserve both sides of that boundary.

## Verification

Verified source: `{{PUBLISHED_HEAD}}`, tree `e0047690e8b0f0013c4e5f3a646ee9663fecb77d`, additive child of `38d586ae`. Actual base checked before publication: `84e5ff153f781c7e2d02804a5c24997858f618ab`.

- [Current-head preparation](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45963141716): the maintained head fails 30 of 124 frozen classifier cases, including both new findings; the reconciled candidate passes all 124. Original source is restored after controls.
- [Full current-source Linux gate](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45964436559): `dune build @fmt`, `dune build --profile release`, and `dune runtest --profile release`, using the required `rd` switch, OCaml 5.5.1 and ocamlformat 0.29.0. {{LINUX_RESULT}}
- [Actual Windows proof](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45957479981): formatting, the full release build, 40 selected shell/permission tests, and 55 native Cmd observations passed on tree `457cd4529dbca9dfb84a258f6a4854b3ce5c6ac2`. The current Linux proof authenticates that artifact and verifies every non-test blob/mode plus the Windows permission fixture is identical. Only the merged test file differs; that new test-only tree was not rerun on Windows. This is not a full Windows-suite claim.
- Native observations include [37 Cmd cases](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45947106831), [50 POSIX cases](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45948949283), [18 exact FOR-option cases](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45955429909), and [14 current-head POSIX boundary cases](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45962135575). The first Cmd observation run failed three initial output hypotheses; its complete observations are retained and later replayed successfully. Setup, transport, and earlier fd integration failures remain separate historical records.

Exact source hashes, artifact digests, source restoration, test preservation, and terminal status are retained in the [proof checkpoint](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/blob/{{CHECKPOINT_COMMIT}}/ci-records/charamel32-current.json). These results establish the tested parser and approval boundaries, without claiming complete Cmd or POSIX shell parity.

The ten earlier review threads were resolved externally. This update addresses the two later scalar-fallback and `env` argument-boundary findings. Ordinary PR CI: {{ORDINARY_CI}}.

replies.text:
Fixed in `{{PUBLISHED_HEAD}}` (tree `e0047690e8b0f0013c4e5f3a646ee9663fecb77d`). The field-expansion decision is made at the actual parameter expression after `${`; literal `{@` or `{!CHAR32_PREFIX@` in a scalar fallback is not treated as an `@` parameter.

The [frozen native Bash/Dash observations](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45962135575) show the reported fallback and its indirect-looking adjacent control each produce one field, while genuine multi-field expansions retain their controls. The [current-head preparation](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45963141716) reproduces the false review on `38d586ae` and passes all 124 classifier cases on the reconciled source. All external test additions are retained apart from the separately native-justified `env` expectation.

The [full Linux source gates](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45964436559) passed on this exact tree. Production bytes and the Windows approval fixture are identical to the [successful native Windows proof](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45957479981), as verified by the current proof; the merged test-only tree itself was not rerun on Windows.

Fixed in `{{PUBLISHED_HEAD}}` (tree `e0047690e8b0f0013c4e5f3a646ee9663fecb77d`). `env` option scanning stops when assignments begin. A lone `-` before assignments retains its option meaning; after an assignment it is the literal executable, so later arguments are not reclassified as the program.

The [native boundary proof](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45962135575) uses owned harmless executables named `-`, `-i`, and `brew.exe` and records which program actually ran. It covers assignments, preceding options, and both sides of the lone-dash boundary. The external test expecting Blocked for the reported command is corrected to Clear from that evidence; ordinary permission/read-only policy still applies.

The [124-case preparation](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45963141716) reproduces the current-head mismatch and passes the repaired source, including the refused-executable controls before assignments. The [full Linux format/build/test gates](https://github.com/gosuda/sloplint/actions/runs/45964436559) passed on the exact published tree. The PR body now states the option-versus-executable distinction explicitly.

original_pr_body:
Follow-up for the unresolved review threads of merged pull requests
#30, #12 and #3, and for the review of this pull request.

Windows shell screen (Cmd dialect):

- #30: a for header with no do cleared the loop. FOR /F with a command
  source cleared the loop. Both fixed here; a set that starts with
  %FILES% is pinned as Review.
- A bare for with no header no longer opens a pending loop, and the
  body delimiter is the first do after the loop set closes, so
  `cmd /c echo ready for review` screens Clear.

POSIX wrapper parsing:

- `env` skips a lone `-` in every position, as GNU env does, so a
  refused executable after other options is blocked, not cleared.
- `command` accepts grouped lookup switches (`command -pv git`).
- Quoted `${@}`, `${@:n}` and `${!prefix@}` expand to one word per
  element and stay under review in env assignments and find operands.

Read-only classification:

- `fd` recognizes attached filter values (`fd -tf`, `--type=f`) as
  data, so plain file searches are read-only while an attached filter
  followed by an execution action stays mutable.

Already fixed or carried, no change here: #12 `shell_screen.ml:1240`
(#30 commit 346ea2c), #3 `test_cli.ml:134` (open #26).

This branch also contains the head of open #20.

Evidence: each new verdict row fails before its fix and passes after.
`dune build @fmt`, `dune build --profile release` and
`dune runtest --profile release` pass (221 tests).

See also: #30, #12, #3
